citations.narrative:
No artificial cooling was provided to the six rabbits when the ambient temperature was greater than 90 degrees F.
Temperature readings in the rabbit area were between 95.5 and 100 degrees F, and the area was under Extreme heat
warnings.
Excessive heat can cause discomfort, overheating, distress and illness.
When the atmospheric temperature exceeds 90degrees F, artificial cooling must be provided to the rabbits.
To be corrected by 7/14/2026.

Excessive amounts of fecal pellets were present on the ground beneath the wooden hutch and between two of the wire
pens of 5 rabbits.
Build up of fecal and waste material can cause distress, illness, disease, odor or attract pests. The floors underneath
primary enclosures with mesh/wire floors should be cleaned and fecal material removed at least once each week.
To be corrected by 7/20/2026.

A Prairie dog was found dead in its cage on the evening of July 12, 2026. The air conditioner in the shed where it was
housed was not functioning and temperatures inside the shed were >115 degrees F at the time it was discovered.
Afternoon high ambient temperatures reached 107 degrees F on July 12, 2026.
Excessive temperatures can cause discomfort, stress, illness and death in animals.
Temperatures in indoor housing facilities must be regulated by heating or cooling to protect the animals from extremes in
temperature. The ambient temperature shall not fall below or rise above temperatures compatible with the health and
comfort of the animal.
No covered animals were housed in the shed at the time of inspection.
To be corrected from this day forward, 7/13/2026.

Several water tubs and buckets in pens containing the 4 Kune-kune pigs and 2 raccoons had large amounts of debris,
slime, and sludge accumulating on the bottom of the water containers and the water was cloudy and dark with floating
debris. The 4 pigs only had one water source and the large pig was standing completely in the tub. The raccoon water
buckets had large amounts of dirt and debris caked onto the sides above the water line.
Dirty water tubs can contaminate the water leading to reduced water intake, illness or death.
All water receptacles shall be kept clean and sanitary.

The two raccoon pen had a large pile of feces accumulated on the ground in front of the feeder. Feed pellets covered the
adjacent section of ground.
The capybara enclosure had a large pile of feces that had been removed from the pool and dumped on the ground within
the enclosure rather than being removed and disposed of appropriately.
Excessive feces can contaminate the animals, increase disease and pest hazards, and increase odors.
Feces should be removed from the enclosures as often as necessary to prevent contamination of the animals, and
minimize disease risks and odors.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
